case_studies.title: Skill-RM: Unifying Heterogeneous Evaluation Criteria via Agent Skill
case_studies.abstract: Reward models (RMs) provide critical feedback signals for LLM post-training, notably in reinforced fine-tuning (RFT) and reinforcement learning (RL) pipelines. However, current reward evaluation relies on heterogeneous criteria such as rule-based verifiers, ground-truth references, procedural checklists, and complex rubrics, where a unified mechanism to integrate all types of evidence remains unexplored. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of integrating different evaluation criteria for reward models in AI training, the authors built a unified framework called Skill-RM, and the result is a more efficient way to provide feedback signals. This could improve the performance of large language models. The research focuses on AI model training and not directly on cloud infrastructure management.

case_studies.title: Taiji: Pareto Optimal Policy Optimization with Semantics-IDs Trade-off for Industrial LLM-Enhanced Recommendation
case_studies.abstract: Scaling recommender systems via large language models (LLMs) has become a prominent trend in the industry. However, aligning the LLM's semantic space with the recommender's ID space via post-training (e.g., SFT and RL) remains challenging. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of aligning large language models with recommender systems, and the result is a new system called Taiji that improves recommendation quality. Taiji was built to address issues with measuring and improving the quality of recommendations in open-domain systems. The result is a more effective way to optimize policy for industrial recommendation systems.

case_studies.title: FLARE: Fine-Grained Diagnostic Feedback for LLM Code Refinement
case_studies.abstract: Large language models often generate code with bugs. Existing methods rely on feedback signals such as test failures and self-critiques to iteratively refine the generated code. Such signals are either too coarse-grained or too high-level, which is not sufficient to inform the model where to fix the bug. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of large language models generating buggy code by creating a framework called Flare that provides fine-grained diagnostic feedback to refine the code. The result is a more efficient and accurate way to identify and fix bugs in generated code. This affects IT work in terms of improving the reliability of automated code generation tools.

case_studies.title: Synthesize and Reward -- Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Step Tool Use in Live Environments
case_studies.abstract: Training LLMs to orchestrate multi-step tool calls is held back by three coupled obstacles: realistic stateful execution environments are costly to build, synthetic training queries are often detached from the server's actual state (so the generated tool calls fail to execute), and recall-based RL rewards incentivize verbose tool-calling patterns. We present PROVE (Programmatic Rewards On Verified Environments), a framework with three contributions: (1) a library of 20 stateful MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers exposing 343 tools, enabling live-execution RL training with session-scoped stat
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of training large language models to use multiple tools in a live environment by building a framework called PROVE, which allows for realistic and efficient training. The result is a library of stateful servers that can be used for live-execution reinforcement learning training. This research may not be directly relevant to managing cloud infrastructure.

case_studies.title: PyraMathBench: Evaluating and Improving Mathematical Capability in Large Language Models
case_studies.abstract: Despite the pivotal role of numerical reasoning as the cornerstone of mathematical capabilities in large language models (LLMs) across applications, few benchmarks evaluate LLMs by integrating numerical processing and mathematical reasoning, hindering the interpretability of failures in math tasks. We introduce PyraMathBench, a comprehensive hierarchical benchmark with 32,505 questions derived from 7,404 math word problems, spanning 4 key cognitive aspects, 14 subcategories, and 2 modalities. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of evaluating mathematical capabilities in large language models by building a comprehensive benchmark called PyraMathBench, which reveals that language models' performance is severely compromised by inadequate numerical computation. The result is a better understanding of language models' limitations in mathematical tasks. This research is not directly relevant to IT infrastructure work.

case_studies.title: Visual Instruction Tuning Aligns Modalities through Abstraction
case_studies.abstract: Visual instruction tuning effectively adapts a pre-trained Large Language Model (LLM) to process image information alongside text. Yet, it remains unclear how visual features are embedded into the layer-wise hierarchy of abstractions of the LLM backbone. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of integrating visual information into large language models, by building a method called visual instruction tuning that adapts pre-trained models to process images and text together, resulting in better alignment of visual and text features. The researchers found that visual features are embedded into intermediate semantic layers of the model. This research is not directly relevant to cloud infrastructure management.

case_studies.title: Agent libOS: A Library-OS-Inspired Runtime for Long-Running, Capability-Controlled LLM Agents
